'''Gary Dwayne Payton II''' (born December 1, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). As a junior and senior playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]], Payton was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] as well as [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Letourneau|first=Connor|title=Gary Payton II, Oregon State Beavers guard, named first team All-Pac-12, Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year|date=March 9, 2015|newspaper=The Oregonian|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2015/03/gary_payton_ii_oregon_state_be_3.html#incart_2box|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref> He won his first [[NBA championship]] with the Warriors in 2022.

Nicknamed "'''GP2'''" and "'''Young Glove'''", Payton is the son of Hall of Famer [[Gary Payton]], known as "'''The Glove'''" in his playing days.<ref name = "Gary Payton II Bio">{{cite web|title=Gary Payton II Bio|work=osubeavers.com|url=http://www.osubeavers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209672849&DB_OEM_ID=30800}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last1= Thompson II | first1= Marcus |title=Young Glove and The Glove, a fit forged through tough love and time |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3241385/2022/04/15/gary-payton-young-glove-golden-state-warriors-nba-playoffs/ | work=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=May 13, 2022 | date=April 15, 2022}}</ref> He is also called "The Mitten", but personally prefers Young Glove.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gary Payton II Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/paytoga02.html |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Rusty |date=2021-11-04 |title=Call him 'Young Glove,' 'Mitten,' or just Gary: Warriors recognize Payton's game |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/Call-him-Little-Glove-Mitten-or-16593134.php |access-date=2022-06-19 |work=San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |author=NBA on TNT |author-link=NBA on TNT |user=NBAonTNT |number=1460800430087225344 |date=November 17, 2021 |title="And what do they call Gary Payton's son?" 👀😂 The son of the glove is... https://t.co/Y6GcbYUHDZ https://t.co/WW64AuM8Sg |access-date=December 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117024228/https://twitter.com/NBAonTNT/status/1460800430087225344 |archive-date=November 17, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gary Payton II prefers a nickname that's an homage to his Hall-of-Fame dad |url=https://fansided.com/2021/11/18/gary-payton-ii-prefers-nickname-thats-homage-hall-fame-dad/ |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=fansided.com}}</ref>

==High school and college career==
Payton was born in [[Seattle]] to Monique and [[Gary Payton]], while his father was a member of the [[Seattle SuperSonics]]. He attended [[Spring Valley High School (Nevada)|Spring Valley High School]] where he lettered two years in basketball and one year in swimming before graduating in 2011. He then enrolled at [[Westwind Preparatory Academy]] for the 2011–12 season.

===Salt Lake Bruins===
Payton played two seasons at [[Salt Lake Community College]] in [[Salt Lake City|Salt Lake City, Utah]]. He averaged 9.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 1.9 steals per game as a freshman (2012–13) and led the Bruins to a 29–5 overall record and 14–1 mark in the [[Scenic West Athletic Conference|Scenic West Athletic Conference (SWAC)]], where they won the Region 18 Championship and outright SWAC title in 2013. Payton was named First Team All-SWAC and made Region 18 All-Tournament Team as a freshman. In his sophomore year, he averaged 14.1 points, 7.9 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 1.9 steals per game, earning him Second Team [[National Junior College Athletic Association|NJCAA]] Division I All-American honors, and was voted 2014 Region 18 Co-Player of the Year and Region 18 Tournament Most Valuable Player. The Bruins finished with a 27–7 overall record and won their second consecutive Region 18 Championship.<ref name = "Gary Payton II Bio"/>

===Oregon State Beavers===
[[File:Gary Payton II Beavers (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Payton with [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] in 2015]]
During Payton's sophomore season at Salt Lake CC he signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] to play for his father's [[alma mater]] [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] under coach [[Craig Robinson (basketball)|Craig Robinson]].<ref>{{cite news|author=Oregonian Sports|title=Oregon State basketball: Gary Payton II signs letter of intent with Beavers|date=November 18, 2013|newspaper=The Oregonian|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2013/11/oregon_state_basketball_gary_p_1.html|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref> Robinson was fired before the start of the 2014–15 basketball season and was replaced by [[Montana Grizzlies basketball|University of Montana]] head coach [[Wayne Tinkle]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Prince|first=Seth|title=Craig Robinson fired as Oregon State Beavers men's basketball coach|date=May 5, 2014|newspaper=The Oregonian|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2014/05/craig_robinson_fired_as_oregon.html|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Mizell|first=Gina|title=Oregon State Beavers officially announce Wayne Tinkle hired as men's basketball coach|date=May 19, 2014|newspaper=The Oregonian|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2014/05/oregon_state_beavers_officiall.html|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref> Having lost their top five scorers from the previous season, Pac-12 coaches picked Oregon State to finish 12th in the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Letourneau|first=Connor|title=In ESPN poll, Pac-12 coaches pick Oregon State men's basketball last in conference|date=October 7, 2014|newspaper=The Oregonian|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2014/10/in_espn_poll_pac-12_coaches_pi.html|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref> Instead, the up-tempo Beavers finished 7th with a 4–1 record against the conference's top three teams, Arizona, Oregon and Utah. In their game against [[Grambling State Tigers men's basketball|Grambling State]], Payton recorded 10 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists, becoming only the second Beaver ever with a [[Double (basketball)#Triple-double|triple-double]] in a game. His father, [[List of players in the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Famer]] [[Gary Payton]], is the other Beaver with a triple-double when he had 20 points, 14 rebounds and 11 assists against the [[Portland Pilots|University of Portland]] in 1988.<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 15, 2014 |title=Gary Payton II joins dad as only Oregon St. players with triple-double |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400593223 |access-date=March 9, 2015 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Following a home sweep of the [[UCLA–USC rivalry|Los Angeles schools]] Payton was named the January 26, 2015 [[2014–15 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12 Conference Player of the Week]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Letourneau|first=Connor|title=Gary Payton II, Oregon State Beavers guard, earns Pac-12 Player of the Week honors|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2015/01/gary_payton_ii_oregon_state_be.html|date=January 26, 2015|newspaper=The Oregonian|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref> During his first season at Oregon State Payton led his team in multiple categories: scoring, rebounds, and steals.<ref>{{cite news|title=Oregon State Season Statistics|date=March 4, 2015|url=http://www.osubeavers.com/fls/30800/MBB/Stats/2014-15/teamcume.htm?DB_OEM_ID=30800|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141226095903/http://www.osubeavers.com/fls/30800/MBB/Stats/2014-15/teamcume.htm?DB_OEM_ID=30800|archive-date=December 26, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 9, 2015, Pac-12 coaches voted Payton to the [[2014–15 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|All-Pac-12 First Team]], [[2014–15 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|All-Pac-12 Defensive Team]] and named him the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]].<ref name = "All-Pac-12 Team">{{cite news|last=Pac-12 Conference|title=2014-15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 9, 2015|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2015/3/9/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref>

On February 1, 2016, he was named one of 10 finalists for the [[Bob Cousy Award]] for top point guard of the year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Nortlander|first1=Matt|title=Cat Barber, Fred VanVleet missing from list of Cousy Award finalists|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25468790/cat-barber-fred-vanvleet-conspicuously-missing-from-cousy-award-finalists|access-date=February 2, 2016|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 1, 2016}}</ref> He was named to the 35-man mid-season watchlist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Player of the Year]] on February 11.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2016–2017)===
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Payton II joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]]. On September 23, 2016, he signed with the Rockets,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-announce-training-camp-roster|title=Rockets Announce Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 23, 2016|access-date=September 23, 2016}}</ref> but was later waived on October 24 after appearing in six preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-waive-three-players|title=Rockets Waive Three Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> On October 31, 2016, he was acquired by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|first=Anwar|last=Chagollan|url=http://riograndevalley.dleague.nba.com/news/vipers-perform-trade-erie-finalize-training-camp-roster/|title=Vipers perform trade with Erie and finalize training camp roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 2, 2016}}</ref> On December 3, 2016, he scored 51 points on 20-of-29 shooting to go with 11 rebounds in a 140–125 win over the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20161203/rgvlad/|title=Payton II Scores 51 To Power Vipers Past D-Fenders|work=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2016|archive-date=June 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170614194703/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20161203/rgvlad/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2017)===
On April 2, 2017, Payton II signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/bucks-sign-gary-payton-ii-contract|title=BUCKS SIGN GARY PAYTON II TO CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=April 2, 2017|access-date=April 2, 2017}}</ref> He made his debut for the Bucks that night, scoring five points in nine minutes off the bench in a 109–105 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899431|title=Mavericks vs. Bucks – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=April 2, 2017|access-date=April 2, 2017}}</ref> Payton II was waived on October 14 as one of the team's final 2017–18 preseason roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks request waivers on three players|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-request-waivers-three-players|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 14, 2017|date=October 14, 2017}}</ref> On October 17, 2017, Payton II was given a [[two-way contract]] with the Bucks via their [[NBA G League]] affiliate the [[Wisconsin Herd]], meaning he would officially return to Milwaukee for the start of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks Sign Gary Payton II To A Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-gary-payton-ii-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> Payton II would have his first start in the NBA on November 22, 2017, against the [[Phoenix Suns]], playing as the starting small forward for the Bucks that night due to team injuries. While he would end the night early due to an injury of his own, the Bucks would win that night in overtime. On December 13, Payton II was waived from the Bucks in favor of [[Sean Kilpatrick]].

===Los Angeles Lakers (2018)===
On January 15, 2018, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] signed Payton II to a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Gary Payton II|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180115lakers-sign-payton-ii|website=Los Angeles Lakers|access-date=January 15, 2018|date=January 15, 2018}}</ref> Throughout the rest of the season, he split his playing time between the Los Angeles Lakers and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[South Bay Lakers]]. On the final game of the season, Payton scored a career-high 25 points and also posted a career-high 12 rebounds against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He was the last Laker to wear number #23 before [[LeBron James]].

===Return to the Vipers (2018–2019)===
On September 4, 2018, Payton signed a training camp contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN THREE PLAYERS|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/story/2018/9/4/blazers-sign-oliver-onuaku-payton|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 4, 2018|date=September 4, 2018}}</ref> On October 13, 2018, Payton was waived by the Trail Blazers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Waive Oliver, Onuaku, & Payton II|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/story/2018/10/13/trailblazers-waive-oliver-onuaku-payton-ii|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 13, 2018|date=October 13, 2018}}</ref>

On December 12, 2018, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]] announced via [[Twitter]] that they had re-acquired Payton.<ref>{{cite tweet |author=RGV Vipers |author-link=RGV Vipers |user=RGVVipers |number=1072962187365416978 |date=December 12, 2018 |title=#RGVVipers reacquire guard Gary Payton II 💥🔥 #NBAGLeague #NextLevel @nbagleague https://t.co/CLTgjsV6JC |access-date=December 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211226040654/https://twitter.com/rgvvipers/status/1072962187365416978 |archive-date=December 26, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2019)===
On January 21, 2019, Payton signed with the [[Washington Wizards]] on a 10-day contract,<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards sign Gary Payton II to a 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-gary-payton-ii-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 21, 2019|date=January 21, 2019}}</ref> and Payton made his debut for the Wizards on January 22 in a 101–87 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071369|title=Wizards' defense steps up in 101-87 victory over Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=January 22, 2019|access-date=January 23, 2019}}</ref> but was not offered a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gary Payton II: Let go by Washington|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/gary-payton-ii-let-go-by-washington|website=cbssports.com|access-date=January 31, 2019|date=January 31, 2019}}</ref>

===Third stint with the Vipers (2019)===
On February 2, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] announced that they had reacquired Payton.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Vipers Reacquire Gary Payton II|date=February 2, 2019|publisher=Rio Grande Valley Viper|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/vipers-reacquire-gary-payton-ii/n-5444129|access-date=April 22, 2019}}</ref>

===Return to Washington (2019–2020)===
On December 23, 2019, Payton signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wizards sign Gary Payton II|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-gary-payton-ii-12-23-19|date=December 23, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 23, 2019}}</ref> On July 9, 2020, he tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=July 9, 2020|title=Report: Two Wizards players test positive for coronavirus|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/report-wizards-players-thomas-bryant-gary-payton-ii-test-positive-coronavirus|access-date=July 21, 2020|work=NBC Sports Washington}}</ref>

===Raptors 905 (2021)===
On January 11, 2021, Payton was selected 15th overall by the [[Raptors 905]] in [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|the NBA G League draft]],<ref>{{cite web|first1=Soheil|last1=Jamshidi|title=Raptors 905 Select Kevon Harris and Gary Payton II in the 2021 NBA G League Draft.|url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-select-kevon-harris-and-gary-payton-ii-in-the-2021-nba-g-league-draft|date=January 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 11, 2021}}</ref> where he averaged 10.8 points on 55.5 percent shooting from the field, 5.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 2.54 steals in 21.9 minutes per game.<ref name="GS210d">{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/gary-payton-ii-10day-20210419|title=Warriors Sign Guard Gary Payton II to a Second 10-Day Contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 19, 2021|access-date=April 20, 2021}}</ref> At the end of the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|shortened single-site season]] in Orlando, he was named the 2021 [[NBA G League Defensive Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905s-gary-payton-ii-named-2020-21-nba-g-league-defensive-player-of-the-year/ |title=Raptors 905's Gary Payton II Named 2020-21 NBA G League Defensive Player Of The Year |website=G League |date=March 19, 2021}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2021–2022)===
On April 8, 2021, Payton signed a 10-day contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/gary-payton-ii-20210408|title=Warriors Sign Guard Gary Payton II to 10-Day Contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2021|access-date=April 8, 2021}}</ref> On April 19, he signed a second 10-day contract<ref name="GS210d" /> and on May 16, he was signed for the rest of the season and the next season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news-gary-payton-ii-20210516|title=Warriors Sign Guard Gary Payton II|website=NBA.com|date=May 16, 2021|access-date=May 17, 2021}}</ref>

Payton was waived shortly before the start of the 2021–22 NBA season,<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive Bell, Bradley, Mulder and Payton II|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/bell-bradley-mulder-payton-waived-20211015|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 16, 2021}}</ref> but was re-signed by the Warriors on October 19 after he cleared waivers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Gary Payton II To Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-gary-payton-ii-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}</ref> Payton had a breakout season and started the first two games of the [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] semifinals against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. In Game 2, he fractured his left elbow when he went up for a fast-break layup but fell hard after the Grizzlies' [[Dillon Brooks]] chased him down and hit him in the head while he was in the air.<ref>{{cite news|first=Kendra|last=Andrews|title=Golden State Warriors' Gary Payton II expected to miss about a month with fractured elbow, sources say|date=May 4, 2022|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33857742/golden-state-warriors-gary-payton-ii-expected-miss-month-fractured-elbow-sources-say|access-date=May 4, 2022}}</ref>

In Game 5 of the [[2022 NBA Finals|Finals]], Payton posted 15 points, five rebounds and three steals in a 104–94 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wiggins delivers on both ends, Warriors lead NBA Finals 3-2 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401442534 |access-date=June 14, 2022 |website=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2022/06/15/kurtenbach-the-warriors-finally-found-the-right-five-man-combination-will-they-use-it-more-in-game-6/ | title=Kurtenbach: The Warriors finally found the right five-man lineup. Will they use to beat the Celtics and claim the title? | date=15 June 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/Warriors-Draymond-Green-Gary-Payton-II-earn-17239828.php | title=Warriors' Draymond Green, Gary Payton II earn redemption with Game 5 grit | date=14 June 2022 }}</ref> The Warriors went on to win Game 6, where Payton played a major defensive role, and Payton won his first [[NBA championship]]. He and his father became the fifth father-son duo to win an NBA title, with one of the other pairs including Payton's teammate [[Klay Thompson]] and his father, [[Mychal Thompson|Mychal]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Luke|last=Norris|title=How Many Father-Son Combos Have Won NBA Championships?|date=June 17, 2022|work=Sportscasting|url=https://www.sportscasting.com/how-many-father-son-combos-have-won-nba-championships/|access-date=June 20, 2022}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2022–2023)===
On July 6, 2022, Payton signed a three-year, $28 million deal with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-gary-payton-ii|title=Trail Blazers Sign Gary Payton II|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2022}}</ref><ref name="q019">{{cite web | last=Andrews | first=Kendra | title=Payton to join Blazers; 3-year deal, sources say | website=ESPN.com | date=2022-07-01 | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34176737/gary-payton-ii-finalizing-multi-year-deal-portland-trail-blazers-agent-says | access-date=2024-10-15}}</ref> He underwent offseason core muscle surgery, which sidelined him for months. On January 2, 2023, Payton made his Blazers debut, putting up seven points, four assists, two rebounds, and one steal in a 135–106 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2023/01/gary-payton-ii-makes-debut-jerami-grant-scores-36-as-trail-blazers-breeze-to-win-over-detroit-pistons-at-the-buzzer.html|title=Gary Payton II makes debut, Jerami Grant scores 36 as Trail Blazers breeze to win over Detroit Pistons: At the buzzer|website=oregonlive.com|last=Fentress|first=Aaron|date=January 2, 2023|access-date=January 2, 2023}}</ref>

===Return to Golden State (2023–2026)===
On February 9, 2023, Payton was traded back to the [[Golden State Warriors]] alongside two second-round picks in a four-team trade involving the [[Atlanta Hawks]] and [[Detroit Pistons]], sending [[Kevin Knox II]] and five second-round picks to Portland, [[James Wiseman]] to Detroit and [[Saddiq Bey]] to Atlanta and made his debut on March 26, against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-gary-payton-ii-20230209|title=Warriors Acquire Guard Gary Payton II and Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/gary-payton-ii-probable-needed-200328180.html|title=Gary Payton II to make needed Warriors return vs. Timberwolves|work=yahoo.com|date=March 25, 2023}}</ref> On March 6, 2024, Payton surpassed 1,000 career points against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in 125–90 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/warriors/status/1765597490391536051|title=Gary Payton II has reached 1,000 career points ⚡️|work=twitter.com|date=March 6, 2024}}</ref>

On April 26, 2025, in the first round of the [[2025 NBA playoffs|NBA playoffs]], Payton scored a playoff career high of 16 points against the [[Houston Rockets]], to help the [[Golden State Warriors]] take a 2-1 lead in the series.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kroichick |first=Ron |date=April 26, 2025 |title=No Jimmy? Steph Curry gets help from Buddy Hield, Gary Payton II in Game 3 win over Rockets |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/no-jimmy-steph-curry-gets-help-hield-payton-win-20294866.php |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 13, 2025 |work=San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref>

On September 29, 2025, Payton re-signed with the Warriors.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Re-Sign Guard Gary Payton II|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-re-sign-guard-gary-payton-ii-20250929|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2025|access-date=October 4, 2025}}</ref>

On August 1, 2026, Payton re-signed with the Warriors.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Guard Gary Payton II|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/gary-payton-ii-signed-20260801|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2026|access-date=August 2, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On September 1, 2025, it was announced that Payton would be launching a professional skateboard league, with intentions to hold its inaugural season in 2026 in [[Big Bear City, California|Big Bear, California]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gary Payton II gets into the action game as skateboard league founder|url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/46119924/nba-free-agent-gary-payton-ii-founds-skateboard-league|access-date=December 12, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>
